c.tagline: A turquoise coast beneath ancient ruins.

avoid.reason: Resort scams — inflated bar bills, carpet/timeshare touts; drink-spiking in nightlife

hood_desc: The charming walled old town of Antalya with Ottoman-era houses, narrow lanes, boutique hotels and a picturesque marina. Ideal for travelers who love historic atmosphere and seaside character.
A modern resort strip east of the center known for sandy beaches, large all-inclusive hotels and spas. Best suited to beach-focused holidaymakers wanting sun and resort comforts.
A long pebble-and-sand beach district backed by the Beydaglari mountains, with promenades, parks and family attractions. Great for beachgoers who want scenic mountain-meets-sea views.
The lively central district of Antalya covering the modern downtown, shopping and everyday city life. Suits visitors who want to stay near urban amenities and transport.
An upscale golf and beach resort area east of Antalya famed for luxury hotels and championship courses. Perfect for golfers and travelers seeking high-end all-inclusive stays.

water.note: Tap water is treated but bottled or filtered water is recommended for visitors.

transit.pay: Cash is not accepted on board: use an Antalyakart smart card, sold and topped up at kiosks and machines at tram stops, the airport and the bus station, or pay by tapping a contactless bank card on buses and trams (slightly higher fare). Rides cost well under US$1.
transit.hours: The AntRay tram and city buses run roughly 6am to midnight; dolmuş minibuses are frequent during the day.

landmarks: Hadrian's Gate
A well-preserved triple-arched Roman gate from the 2nd century AD, marking the entrance to Antalya's old town.
Kaleiçi (Old Town)
Antalya's historic old quarter of narrow lanes, Ottoman houses, and a picturesque marina ringed by ancient city walls.
Düden Waterfalls
Dramatic falls where freshwater plunges directly into the Mediterranean Sea, a striking natural landmark near the city.
Yivli Minaret Mosque
A distinctive fluted, turquoise-tiled Seljuk-era minaret that has become a symbol of Antalya's skyline.
Antalya Aquarium
One of the world's largest tunnel aquariums, offering vivid, otherworldly underwater photo opportunities.
Termessos
A dramatic ruined ancient city perched high in the mountains above Antalya, prized by photographers for its rugged, untouched setting.
Perge
An extensive ancient Greco-Roman city ruin near Antalya, with a well-preserved stadium and colonnaded streets.
Konyaaltı Beach
A long pebble beach with a backdrop of the Beydağları mountains, offering a classic panoramic view of Antalya's coastline.
Antalya Archaeological Museum
One of Turkey's leading museums, its thirteen halls hold more than five thousand artifacts from Karain Cave finds to Roman-era marble statues and mosaics.
Karaalioğlu Park
A cliffside park at the edge of the old town with palm-lined promenades, sweeping Mediterranean views, and the Roman-era Hıdırlık Tower overlooking the harbor.

train.note: Antalya has no mainline railway station - only a city tram (Antray). The nearest TCDD stations are at Burdur and Isparta (regional trains, ~2-3h north by road) and Konya, which has YHT high-speed trains onward to Ankara and Istanbul. A high-speed line to Antalya is under construction but not yet open, so for now inter-city travel means buses or flights.

bus.note: Antalya's huge Otogar (bus terminal) is a domestic hub, not an international one - long-distance coaches to Europe generally start in Istanbul. Main Turkish operators serving Antalya are Kamil Koc (kamilkoc.com.tr), Metro Turizm (metroturizm.com.tr/en) and Pamukkale (pamukkale.com.tr).

ferry.note: No scheduled international ferry leaves from Antalya itself. The reliable year-round passenger boat to Northern Cyprus (Girne/Kyrenia) sails from Tasucu near Silifke/Mersin (well east of Antalya) and is run by Akgunler Denizcilik (akgunlerbilet.com). A seasonal Alanya-Girne fast ferry (~2h east of Antalya) has run on and off in summers - confirm it is operating before planning around it.
